## Nikon’s Z5IIC Rumors Heat Up

The 4chan photography community is buzzing with renewed interest in the rumored Nikon Z5IIC, positioning it as a direct competitor to Sony’s dominant Z5 and a7c lines. Based on recent leaks, the compact full-frame camera will reportedly feature a 24 MP sensor with in-body image stabilization (IBIS) and run on the Expeed 7 processor. Aesthetically, it is expected to adopt a rangefinder-style silhouette, notably lacking the traditional viewfinder hump.

Community sentiment is deeply split. While some users welcome a genuine alternative to Sony’s compact offerings, others remain skeptical, dubbing it a potential "parts bin camera" or a derivative "Sony sister" model. Common criticisms point toward the anticipated "blobmera" lens configuration and concerns over grip ergonomics. Despite the skepticism, the ongoing discourse highlights a hunger for compact full-frame options that prioritize portability without sacrificing core imaging capabilities.

## Synth Scene: Inventory, Innovation, and Improvisation

The modular synthesizer world saw significant activity across multiple platforms. Perfect Circuit listings highlighted via MATRIXSYNTH brought attention to three key analog units: the Arturia DrumBrute Impact, the Roland Boutique TR-06 Drumatix, and the Arturia MicroBrute UFO. These straightforward inventory drops provided clear focal points for collectors and creators alike.

On the creative front, the MOD WIGGLER community shared new drone compositions, including @lfad’s "Alien Construct No. 01," which incorporates percussion elements into a long-form patch. Meanwhile, two creators showcased the Sequential Fourm synthesizer. kgbirmingham demonstrated preset-based improvisation that retained a distinct lead line, while Tom Leclerc shared a tape-machine recording enhanced with Valhalla reverb, thanking Woodbrass and Sequential for the hardware.

Additionally, Animal Factory Amplification released a detailed breakdown of the Asura, a polyphonic wavetable synth featuring analog fuzz. The video highlighted its extensive control layout, including "Shift" parameters like Detune and Melt FM, offering a deep dive into its sound design potential for enthusiasts.

## AI Regulation: Reality Over Narratives

A compelling argument emerged on Bluesky regarding AI regulation, positing that policy should prioritize technological reality and open access over "x-risk" narratives. The post suggests that dominant firms often misuse safety standards as entry barriers. Key proposals include preventing exclusionary cloud-model bundling, scrutinizing compute-supply agreements, and ensuring data portability to maintain interoperability. The core assertion is that regulations focused on use cases and failures are more urgent than those targeting specific models, with the most critical regulatory actions potentially lacking an "AI" label entirely.

## Technical Debates: MFT vs. Sony Flange Distance

A technical debate on 4chan’s /p/ board focused on Micro Four Thirds (MFT) sensor design. Users contrasted GoPro’s utilization of MFT’s compactness against Olympus and Panasonic, specifically addressing Sony’s shorter flange distance. Critics argued Sony’s "baby mount" causes severe vignetting and oblique photon angles, requiring exposure compensation. Conversely, MFT defenders highlighted its telecentric lens design, which uses an oversized mount to ensure light hits sensor pixels perpendicularly, reducing shading effects. The discussion concluded with a mix of optical physics analysis and community memes regarding lens compatibility.

## Quick Hits

*   **Sony’s Reputation Sinks:** 4chan’s /p/ board is currently dominated by Fujifilm users, leading to a sentiment that Sony is an unpopular "meme" brand. The thread "Innovation is dead Part 2" reinforced the perception that the community has shifted allegiance, pushing back against Sony-centric discussions.
*   **Analog Delay Demo:** Laurent Baloran uploaded a test video for MATRIXSYNTH demonstrating the Proto II and The River II. The setup uses VCAs to manage mix and feedback, allowing the dry signal to remain purely analog while digital processing handles the delay.
*   **San Diego Design Week 2026:** Social media is highlighting the upcoming event, featuring 200 artists and designers. A KPBS article details 15 free ways to explore the week-long celebration, showcasing abstract artwork in modern gallery spaces with polished wooden floors and exposed trusses.
*   **Personal Setups:** Users shared aesthetic workspace tours, ranging from a streamlined gaming/studio hybrid with an Xbox controller and Hennessy decor to a dense Eurorack station in cherry wood racks, balancing technical complexity with personal style.

@4528705 - /p/ — >Tfw GoPro is the only company actually taking advantage of mfourturds being small — >>4528702 >physical truths like Sony E being a baby mount are forced memes now The so-called Leica-esque lenses vignette even worse on Sony lol, let alone adapted Leica lenses. Sony cameras push exposure on the outer edges to compensate for the massive vignetting, sometimes 2 stops. The same short flange you brag about causes extreme incident angles that bring vignetting. The photons simply hit the array too obliquely to enter the photosites. That's why MFT uses a telecentric design and has a seemingly oversized mount. That's why Leicas have special microlenses too.  This is a technical diagram comparing the internal structures of a "Leica M240" sensor versus a "Traditional sensor," illustrating how light is processed in each. The diagram is set against a black background. On the left, under the white title "Leica M240," a cross-section shows three adjacent pixel units. Each unit consists of a gray "Pixel" base, a "Photodiode" layer, a colored "Color filter" layer (Green, Red, and Purple from left to right), and a "Microlens" on top. White arrows representing "Incoming light" pass through the microlenses and are directed straight down onto their corresponding photodiodes without obstruction. On the right, under the title "Traditional sensor," a similar cross-section of three pixel units is shown. These also have "Pixel," "Photodiode," "Color filter" (Green, Red, and Purple), and "Microlens" layers. However, white rectangular barriers between the photodiodes cause some of the "Incoming light" (indicated by white and red arrows) to hit the side of the photodiode or be blocked before it reaches the sensor, a phenomenon often referred to as the "shading effect" or "microlens shading." The diagram uses red arrows on the right side specifically to highlight this light loss and redirection.

clusters.summary: 4chan users are debating the technical merits of Micro Four Thirds (MFT) sensor designs, specifically focusing on GoPro’s unique utilization of the format's compactness compared to competitors like Olympus and Panasonic. A key argument centers on the MFT mount’s size, with one user claiming Sony’s shorter flange distance creates a "baby mount" that causes severe vignetting and oblique photon angles, requiring exposure compensation. In contrast, defenders of MFT highlight its telecentric lens design, which utilizes an oversized mount to ensure light hits sensor pixels perpendicularly, reducing the shading effects seen in traditional sensors. This technical distinction is illustrated by a diagram comparing the internal pixel structures of a Leica M240 against a traditional sensor, emphasizing how MFT’s design mitigates light loss. The discussion concludes with a mix of technical analysis on optical physics and community memes, such as the "baby mount" label, regarding lens compatibility and sensor performance.
